title: Exhaustion Pace and Extension Visits on Visit Referrals
content:
When an In-Group Specialist Referral, an HMO Specialist Referral, an Out-of-Network Referral or a Physical Therapy Episode Authorization (Referrals & Prior Authorizations) is extended, the exhaustion-pace adjustment of the extension visits follows how quickly the referral was used up: an exhausted referral whose most recent unit use came within 60 days of its latest decision adds two visits; an exhausted referral whose most recent use came later than that but within 90 days of that decision adds one visit; any other referral adds nothing.

## Questions answered

**How is the pace measured?** As the calendar days from the referral's latest decision date, as recorded on the referral, to the date of the most recent unit use on its ledger.

**Exhausted, most recent use 60 days after the latest decision?** Within 60 days: two visits added.

**Exhausted, most recent use 61 days after?** Later than 60 but within 90: one visit added.

**Exhausted, most recent use 90 days after?** Within 90: one visit added. At 91 days, nothing is added.

**An approved referral that still has visits?** It is not exhausted, so nothing is added whatever its pace.
